correctness.rationale: The dual has full 2-skeleton and tetrahedra exactly the connected four-sets. For odd n the torus need not be bipartite, but the needed assertion is local: any closed walk of length <=5 has zero column winding for n>=6, and even row-step parity; thus any induced five-vertex graph here is bipartite. If all its four-vertex deletions are connected its minimum degree is two or more, forcing K_{2,3}, which the product excludes since no distinct pair has three common neighbors. The triangle-free four-set count is 16n stars, 52n induced paths and 5n squares. Independently using the 35 cycle coordinates complementary to a cube vertex, the 35x38 cube boundary has 35 unit Smith factors. I also independently checked the 36 supplied templates as data, enumerating connected tetrahedron translation types and retaining actual coface offsets on the infinite strip; there are 73 types, of which 37 survive in the consecutive-column cubes, and each chosen triangle is free at its removal and outside those cubes. The cyclic cases 6–13 reproduced. For a uniform check, lift each connected tetrahedron to a strip window of span <=3. For n>=7, two such lifts meeting in a projected triangle, aligned at one common vertex, agree on its other vertices: each difference from the aligned vertex is in [-3,3], whose residues are distinct. No wrap-around changes incidences or the template orbits, with n=6 checked directly. The cube union glued along full single-column simplices has H_3=Z^{3n}, H_2=0. Adding only relative cells of dimension <=2 after collapse preserves H_3 and embeds H_2 into free relative H_2. Simple connectivity and Euler characteristic then give the wedge; alternatively use the saturated integral attaching matrix of the 3-cells over the full 2-skeleton, a wedge of two-spheres. Duality gives degrees 4n-6 and 4n-5, and the lower of those groups excludes pure shellability of the original.
residual_risks: No assertion for n<6, other widths, total cuts or the original cut complex's homotopy type. The graph itself is not generally bipartite, but the needed local property is proved above.
